scripts.//-- setup --: One-time bootstrap: install deps, start local Postgres (:5434), apply migrations, load the synthetic quaternary and gauging-station datasets (the catchment map's lookups) and the synthetic register of dams (its dam proposals), start Mailpit (:8026) and MinIO (:9002, PDF reports). See docs/run-locally.md.
scripts.setup: pnpm install && pnpm dev:db:up && pnpm dev:db:migrate && pnpm import:quaternaries && pnpm import:gauge-stations && pnpm import:dam-register && pnpm import:land-cover && pnpm import:evaporation && pnpm import:rivers && pnpm dev:mail:up && pnpm dev:s3:up
scripts.//-- dev --: dev = frontend (:7777) + backend (:3001) in parallel. dev, dev:full, dev:run:backend and dev:run:worker start Postgres first (dev:db:up; a no-op when it is already up); Mailpit and MinIO stay opt-in (dev:mail:up, dev:s3:up). The background-job worker is opt-in: dev:full = dev + the worker, or dev:run:worker on its own (JOB_TRANSPORT=inprocess: polls the job table every 15 s and wakes on LISTEN job_queued; Postgres only, no AWS). dev:jobs:tick runs one tick (every due job) and exits. dev:all starts everything: Mailpit, MinIO with the map's basemap when one is cached (bin/tiles-dev.sh up --cached: never fetches), then dev:full (Postgres, frontend, backend, worker). Ctrl+C stops the app; dev:down then stops every container (Postgres, Mailpit, MinIO; the volumes and their data stay; shared by every checkout, worktrees included). dev:feeds:run is one tick that first queues every enabled data feed, due or not (FEED_SOURCE=fixtures by default: synthetic files, no network). dev:ingest:push posts the synthetic logger CSV (scripts/ingest/fixture.csv, re-dated to end yesterday) to the ingest endpoint with the API key in WM_INGEST_KEY (env or the gitignored root .env.development.local; make the key under Settings → API keys). See docs/run-locally.md § Background jobs, § Data feeds and § Ingest.
scripts.dev:all: pnpm dev:mail:up && bin/tiles-dev.sh up --cached && pnpm dev:full
scripts.//-- db --: Local Postgres 17 in docker on :5434 (user/db water, app role water_app). Migrations live in backend/migrations. Each checkout has its own dev database: water in the main checkout, water_w<n> in a git worktree, created on first dev / dev:db:migrate and empty until seed:examples (backend/src/config/devEnv.ts; DEV_DB_NAME overrides), so a branch's unmerged migrations never reach main's. dev:db:migrate and dev:db:psql act on this checkout's; dev:db:reset drops the whole volume, every checkout's databases included.
scripts.dev:db:reset: docker compose down -v && pnpm dev:db:up && pnpm dev:db:migrate
scripts.//-- mail --: Mailpit catches all local email (verify, password reset, invites, alerts): SMTP :1026, web UI http://localhost:8026. The backend's dev default is MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp → Mailpit; see docs/run-locally.md § Email. dev:mail:bounce <email> [--complaint | --transient] stands in for SES's bounce and complaint events (no SES locally): it flags that account's address as suppressed, pausing its alert emails behind the banner on the account and alert pages (needs dev:db:up; docs/run-locally.md § Alerts).
scripts.//-- s3 --: MinIO: S3-compatible storage for server-side PDF reports and evidence packs' reproduction bundles (STORAGE=local, the default; issuing a pack stores its bundle, so it needs MinIO): API :9002, console http://localhost:9003 (minioadmin / minioadmin, dev-only). The backend creates the water-reports and water-packs buckets on first use. The worker renders reports with the Chromium from test:e2e:install; see docs/run-locally.md § Reports.
scripts.//-- tiles --: The catchment map's basemap (issue #288, docs/maps.md § Basemap), optional: without it the map draws its features on a plain background, and CI never downloads tiles. dev:tiles:up starts it in one step, safe to re-run: MinIO, then the cached extract and fonts uploaded if MinIO lacks them (fetched only when nothing is cached), the relief's DEM uploaded only if it is cached (never fetched there), then PUBLIC_TILES_URL, PUBLIC_TILES_GLYPHS_URL (and PUBLIC_TERRAIN_URL when the DEM is served) set in frontend/.env.development.local (restart pnpm dev after). dev:tiles:fetch extracts South Africa from the Protomaps daily build with the pmtiles CLI (go-pmtiles, on PATH) into ~/.cache/water-management-tiles/ (TILES_MAXZOOM, default 15; TILES_BBOX; TILES_BUILD) and uploads it to the local MinIO's tiles bucket (needs dev:s3:up), then the labels' fonts. dev:tiles:fonts fetches only the fonts (Noto Sans glyph ranges, OFL 1.1, from protomaps/basemaps-assets at a pinned commit; no pmtiles CLI). dev:tiles:terrain extracts the relief's DEM (Copernicus GLO-30 as Terrarium tiles, from the Mapterhorn planet build; TERRAIN_MAXZOOM, default 12, ~2.2 GB) into the same cache and bucket (docs/maps.md § Relief). dev:tiles:rivers downloads HydroRIVERS v1.0 (Africa, ~110 MB, licence allows commercial use with attribution), cuts it to TILES_BBOX with ogr2ogr (GDAL) and loads it with import:rivers into this checkout's database as HydroRIVERS-v10 (RIVERS_MIN_ORDER, default 1; needs dev:db:up; docs/maps.md § River network). dev:tiles:status says what is cached and served. dev:tiles:env prints the PUBLIC_TILES_URL, PUBLIC_TILES_GLYPHS_URL and PUBLIC_TERRAIN_URL lines for frontend/.env.development.local.
scripts.//-- data --: Demo data. seed:examples = 3 invented catchments (skipped once they exist) + 2 demo users (demo@ / analyst@example.com) + 2 demo farmers (farmer1@ / farmer2@example.com) + a demo applicant with a submitted application (applicant@example.com), password demo-password, works on any clone. seed:demo = seed:examples + each client workbook in ../project-water-management-source/Original/ (WBT_SOURCE_DIR) as its own project, named from its file name at run time, skipping any the demo user already has (needs Python + openpyxl, scripts/wbt-import/README.md); a workbook's gauge column is imported as a reference gauge, with per-workbook settings in wbt-import.<prefix>.env beside the workbooks (bin/seed-demo.sh; WBT_SETTINGS / WBT_FIT=1 patch the settings and fit GR4J at import, docs/model.md §2.10b). seed:demo:fixed = the same from the fixed workbooks in ../project-water-management-source/Fixed/workbooks/ (the review's formula fixes, recalculated), each as "<Name> (fixed)" beside the original. pan-sensitivity takes any project.json (no DB): GR4J at a few pan-coefficient choices, fixed vs refitted, written to a Markdown table (docs/model.md §2.4a). fit-sweep <project.json> --grid <grid.json> fits GR4J once per cell of a grid of fit settings (pan preset × bounds × objective × named exclusion set × WR2012 band on/off), with validation, and writes one Markdown table (and --json), ranking nothing (no DB; at most 24 cells unless --max-cells; docs/model.md §2.10b). Both resolve paths from where you typed the command; a report on the client catchment stays in the gitignored data/client-catchment/, never committed. reproduce:pack <bundle.zip> [--expect <manifest hash>] [--no-run] [--json] checks an evidence pack's reproduction bundle (downloaded from the pack) and re-runs its runs with this checkout's engine: every file against its hash, the manifest against the pack's hash, then each run's results digest; exit 0 when it reproduces, 1 on a mismatch (no DB, no network; scripts/reproduce-pack/reproduce-pack.ts, docs/evidence-pack.md § Reproduction). It resolves its path from where you typed the command too. import:quaternaries loads the quaternary dataset the catchment map's lookup proposes the WR2012 check's values from (issue #288, docs/maps.md § Quaternary dataset), as the schema owner: with no argument the committed synthetic one (region Z, invented values), else <boundaries.geojson> --dataset <label> --source "<study>" [--values <values.csv>], the operator's own DWS/WR2012 download (never committed); a load replaces its dataset (needs dev:db:up). import:gauge-stations loads the gauging stations the map proposes as the observed-flow source (issue #326, docs/maps.md § Gauging stations), the same way: with no argument the committed synthetic ones (region Z, invented), else <stations.geojson|.csv> … --dataset <label> --source "<catalogue, URL, date>" (the DWS catalogue, once its licence is confirmed; never committed). import:dam-register loads the register of dams the dam proposals read (issue #326 B-dams, docs/maps.md § Dams from the register and the map), as the schema owner: with no argument the committed synthetic list (register numbers Z…, invented dams), else <list.csv> <overlay.kml> [<dams.json>] --dataset <label> --source "<list, edition>", the operator's own DSO download (never committed; its licence is unconfirmed); a load replaces its dataset (needs dev:db:up). import:land-cover loads the cropland grid the planted-area proposals read (issue #326 B-landcover, docs/maps.md § Cultivated area from land cover), as the schema owner: with no argument the committed synthetic grid (invented), else <tile.tif> … --dataset <label> [--cell 0.0025] [--bbox w,s,e,n], the operator's own ESA WorldCover tiles (CC BY 4.0; never committed), pre-summarised into cells at import so the app reads no raster; a load replaces its dataset (needs dev:db:up). import:rivers loads the river network the Map tab's River network layer draws and proposes river features from (issue #345, docs/maps.md § River network), as the schema owner: with no argument the committed synthetic network (invented reaches), else <rivers.geojson> … --dataset <label> --source "<product, version, attribution>" [--min-order <n>] (dev:tiles:rivers runs it for HydroRIVERS; never committed); a load replaces its dataset (needs dev:db:up). import:evaporation loads the evaporation grid the Settings proposal of GR4J's PE (or the A-pan row) reads (issue #326 B-evap, docs/maps.md § Evaporation from the map), as the schema owner: with no argument the committed synthetic grid (invented), else <file> … --dataset <label> [--bbox w,s,e,n]: dPET years (.nc, or the totals --reduce <dir> wrote), averaged into monthly means; import:evaporation:fetch [first] [last] downloads dPET (CC BY 4.0; about 2.4 GB a year, deleted once reduced; never committed) and loads it; a load replaces its dataset (needs dev:db:up).
scripts.//-- gen --: Generated assets, committed. gen:help-art renders the help pictures (one Blender scene, several shots) with Blender 5 + ImageMagick 7 (optional tooling; scripts/help-art/catchment.py; HELP_ART_ONLY=shot,… for some). gen:landing-art regenerates everything the public landing page shows (issue #57, docs/design/landing-art.md): the diorama lit for day and dusk (Blender, the help scene), contours, icons and device frames (Inkscape), AVIF/WebP and the social card (ImageMagick, avifenc, FontForge), the app screens (Playwright on the example catchments; needs dev:db:up) and the charts and what-if grid (the engine); optional tooling, LANDING_ART_ONLY=render,vector,screens,data for some steps, LANDING_ART_DEVICE for the GPU. gen:example rewrites frontend/src/lib/components/projects/exampleCatchment.generated.json, the invented Kleinberg example catchment the empty project list's Start from an example imports (issue #286; backend/scripts/example-file.ts, no database, ~10 s for its GR4J fit); backend/scripts/example-file.test.ts fails until you rerun it after changing the example catchments or the model's fields. gen:dem-fixture rewrites backend/fixtures/dem/synthetic-dem.pmtiles, the invented DEM delineation is tested against (issue #326 B-delineate; terrain in backend/src/delineation/fixture.ts, no database); backend/scripts/dem-fixture.test.ts fails until you rerun it after changing the terrain. gen:liability rewrites the generated liability modules in packages/engine/src/liability/ (WP-3.13): limitations.generated.ts from docs/engine-audit.md (the open audit items a validation statement and a sign-off list), errata.generated.ts from docs/engine-errata.md (known bugs per engine version) and methodology*.generated.ts from docs/methodology/v<N>.md (each version's SHA-256, the current text); each has a test that fails until you rerun it after changing its doc. gen:i18n:sheet [lang…] rewrites docs/i18n/<code>-translation-sheet.md, the strings a farmer sees that have no reviewed words yet in that language, read from the frontend's t() / msg() / plural() calls (WP-2.5; docs/ui.md § Language), and frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/ids.generated.ts, every message's id (default: every non-English language in packages/engine/src/languages.ts); rerun it after adding or changing a message or a translation. gen:i18n:stamp <lang> <id> re-stamps a farmer glossary translation's sourceHash from the current English once the translator has re-checked it (and rewrites that language's sheet). gen:i18n:export <lang> <dir> writes that language's sheet rows as JSON batches for translation (the i18n-translator agent, .claude/agents/i18n/); gen:i18n:apply <lang> <id→words.json …> checks returned translations (placeholders, bold, whole plurals and glossary entries) and writes them into that language's three catalogues (creating one that doesn't exist yet), then rewrites its sheet. gen:e2e:timings replaces e2e/shard-timings.json, the per-test durations CI's e2e shards are packed from, with the e2e-timings artifact of the newest green CI run on main (needs gh; commit the result when the shards drift apart; a test without a timing is planned at the median, so it's never urgent; e2e/README.md § CI). gen:bundle-budget <slug> <kb> "<why>" raises (or, negative, lowers) the frontend's total bundle ceiling by writing one entry file, scripts/guards/bundle-budget/<today>-<slug>.json, which check:bundle adds to the frozen base; never edit BUDGET.totalCodeKb, so parallel PRs never conflict on it (scripts/guards/bundle-budget/README.md).
scripts.//-- build --: Production builds: static frontend (frontend/build) and the Lambda bundle (backend/dist/lambda.mjs).
scripts.//-- check --: Typecheck every workspace, plus the repo guards CI runs: committed env files stay local (check:env), the Claude agents and commands cite only real paths and no template placeholders (check:claude), workflow pins/OIDC/gate rules + actionlint (check:workflows), frontend bundle ceilings (check:bundle, after build:frontend; the total is a base plus scripts/guards/bundle-budget/'s entries, gen:bundle-budget), advisory privacy-doc drift vs origin/main (check:compliance), no client-identifying term in any tracked file or path (check:terms; needs ../infra-secrets/water-management/client-terms.txt, else a no-op), every language's translation sheet is current and no glossary translation is stale (check:i18n lists what is untranslated or stale, for every language; fix with gen:i18n:sheet / gen:i18n:stamp <lang> <id>). The five Playwright pins agree and are exact (check:pins: backend and renderer-deps playwright-core, its lockfile, e2e's @playwright/test, the renderer image tag; plus the renderer image's base digest and its apt packages at exact versions from one snapshot; scripts/guards/check_playwright_pins.mjs). check:workflows also keeps github_actions and docker off the Dependabot auto-merge allowlist, and the renderer image's npm directory (/backend/renderer-deps) out of auto-merge.
scripts.//-- test --: test:changed = the fast inner loop: typecheck + vitest --changed for only what the working changes touch (seconds; db tests too when :5434 is up; never e2e), see docs/testing.md. test = unit tests everywhere (no DB, no wall-clock assertions; the gate before a commit). test:guards = node:test suites for the CI/release guards in scripts/ and the infra scripts (infra/scripts/restore-db.sh against a fake aws + terraform + sops, infra/scripts/tf.sh against a fake sops + terraform, bin/check-infra.sh against a fake terraform, infra/scripts/preapply-check.sh and postapply-check.sh against a fake aws + curl; needs bash, git and jq). test:backend:db needs dev:db:up; it migrates and uses the water_test database (water_test_w<n> in a git worktree, backend/src/__tests__/test-db.ts). test:engine:perf / test:backend:perf are separate performance-budget targets (median of several runs; not part of `test` because a busy machine or parallel workspaces would make a hard wall-clock ceiling flake — run them alone). test:backend:perf also runs the V8 deopt stress of the assurance of supply (backend model/assurance-jit.perf.test.ts, issue #192): timing-dependent, so run it alone too. test:backend:v8-osr [--rev <git rev>] [--node <binary>] [-- <V8 flags>] is the same stress against the engine at any revision, by default the last one with the day loop V8 miscompiled (47e1ddb1^): exit 1 when a stressed run differs, so it says whether a Node version still has the bug (issue #232, docs/upstream/v8-maglev-osr.md); alone, several minutes, not in CI. test:backend:perf:db is the same for budgets that need Postgres (dev:db:up; it rebuilds the checkout's water_test… like test:backend:db, so never beside it); not in CI either. test:verify = the independent cross-check of the engine (verify/README.md): a Python model written only from the docs, run beside runModel on the example catchments, the probes and random networks, plus its mutation self-test (Python 3.14, stdlib only; ~2–3 min; VERIFY_TEST_RANDOM=<n> / VERIFY_TEST_DENSE=<n> for more random / dense networks, CI runs 200 of each; the report is python3 verify/diff.py --random <n> --dense <n>).
scripts.//-- e2e --: Playwright (Chromium), fully local. Needs dev:db:up; rebuilds its own database and starts its own backend + a production build of the frontend (frontend/build-e2e; dev servers and frontend/build untouched): water_e2e, :3101 and :7801 in the main checkout, a per-worktree slot elsewhere (E2E_SLOT overrides; e2e/support/env.ts), so two checkouts can run it at once. First time: test:e2e:install. See e2e/README.md.
scripts.//-- infra --: Terraform in infra/: credential-free fmt -check + validate + plan-only `terraform test` (mocked providers, tests/guardrails.tftest.hcl). Needs terraform (tfenv, infra/.terraform-version). Never plans against or applies to AWS; see infra/README.md.
scripts.//-- renderer --: The report renderer's container image (backend/renderer.Dockerfile, the release path's image): check:renderer-image packages the Lambdas, builds the image and smoke-tests it as Lambda runs it (Chromium prints a PDF; the handler answers under the Lambda runtime interface emulator, pinned in infra/scripts/smoke-renderer-image.sh; the init check refuses a missing setting). Needs docker; no AWS account; ~3.5 GB image. CI runs the same (ci.yml, renderer-image); see docs/deployment.md § Reports. Its build stage's apt packages are pinned to one Ubuntu archive snapshot (APT_SNAPSHOT) that nothing moves by itself: check:apt-snapshot says how old it is (limit 90 days; renderer-apt-snapshot.yml runs it weekly and opens an issue when stale), and gen:renderer-apt [<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>] moves it (default today) and rewrites every pinned version to its candidate in that snapshot, read with apt-cache in the Dockerfile's digest-pinned base (docker run, no build; needs network). Run gen:renderer-apt whenever the base digest moves (Dependabot's docker PR), then check:pins and check:renderer-image. scripts/guards/renderer_apt_snapshot.mjs.
